Issued at 332 PM EDT Fri Aug 7 2026

PATTERN SYNOPSIS/FORECAST:

Difluent flow over the Upper Midwest this morning...with general 
troughing across the eastern CONUS squeezed between two 597/598dm 
500mb highs:  one over the Desert SW, and the other over Bermuda. 
Upper low over central Canada with several niblets of PV swirling 
through the Canadian Prairies attm, including a shortwave trough 
axis that stretches from central Ontario down into MN and SD. Broad 
return flow across the SE US where better moisture (pwats greater 
than 1.5in) is noted...also sneaking up into the Upper Midwest 
along/ahead of aforementioned trough axis, along with some weaker 
stability aloft oozing out of the central Plains, and this is where 
convective activity is developing this morning. Low level moisture 
remains on the higher side across the Great Lakes attm, with both 
12z/07 MI soundings reporting nearly saturated layers below 600-
700mb below abundant dry air aloft...and quite a bit in the way of 
low clouds/fog around this morning which finally mixed out around 15-
17z; a few showers already popped up across NE Lower as of 13z, and 
diurnal cu already underway elsewhere by noonish with some lake 
breeze development. Nose of 16-20C 850mb temps along and ahead of 
the aforementioned trough axis and attendant surface boundary from 
the Central Plains to Lake Superior and up toward James Bay; low/mid-
levels cool behind this, to 8C across central Canada (even a tiny 
bit of 4C air showing up in northern Manitoba attm). 

Cyclonic flow aloft remains the theme for the bulk of the next seven 
days here in the Upper Great Lakes...with upper low over central 
Canada slowly meandering eastward with time into next week...with 
potential for another lobe to swing down into central Canada toward 
midweek or so...and greater uncertainty in the evolution of the 
forecast beyond this. The bottom line is that it could remain a 
little more on the unsettled side than not through the next several 
days...starting with a boundary draping into the area tonight and 
bringing a shot at showers and thunderstorms into at least part of 
the day Saturday before washing out in the region. This should 
become the focus for additional activity later Saturday night into 
Sunday as another bit of energy swings in...and think this boundary 
will be very slow to move over the next several days, though various 
niblets of energy should slide across it at times. 

FORECAST DETAILS...

Rain/storms tonight into Saturday morning...think our best shot at 
activity tonight will be between 6z to 15z or so, along and ahead of 
the front sliding through...though we should see some activity 
through the evening, especially across NE Lower where there could be 
better instability and the lake breeze for convergence...and across 
the Yoop closer to the forcing and better plume of low-level warm 
advection. The shortwave trough may turn negatively tilted to our 
north as it swings through late tonight/early morning, and this 
could signal a period of better forcing and perhaps a little spicier 
convection with a slight increase in deep-layer shear toward 
morning, esp across the Yoop and a marginal 20-30kt LLJ in the 
vicinity; wouldn't be entirely surprised if we started out the 
morning with some lingering activity. Otherwise, the nocturnal 
timing is not typically great for convection, as we should garner 
some CINH overnight...but think we could still have some low-level 
instability to work with, and 1000-2000J/kg MUCAPE as well. 

Heavy rain concerns ahead???... Stalled/washed-out zonal boundary 
with periodic perturbations and southwesterly flow certainly seems 
like a setup worth keeping an eye on for hydro concerns going 
forward, starting Sunday into Monday ahead of the currently 
anticipated initial wave. Pwats could reach into the 1.5-2 inch 
range which is quite moist; signals also point toward potential for 
some training convection to develop along the perimeter of a plume 
of weak stability to our southwest. Will need to keep a close eye on 
this going forward, as there is potential for the convection to 
track into our area...though it is still possible it could dive to 
our south...which could drag the whole boundary southward and 
perhaps limit our heavy rain concerns. The idea of convection on the 
perimeter of that weak stability axis could also indicate potential 
for stronger thunderstorms late this weekend into early next 
week...and will also be something to keep an eye on, though again, 
better chances could remain to our south.
